scope: Read-only macOS process/file metadata and current public source review; proposed capacity design only. No complete stack load test or Linux qualification.

conclusion.reason: Historical full-block archive, accepted-block digest history and whole-state copies grow with chain history. Segmentation alone would not bound retained disk use or RPC decode memory.

host_observation.method: ps PID/PPID/RSS/executable-name columns; lsof cwd metadata for process attribution; sysctl hardware counts. No process arguments or environment collected. Ephemeral tool observations, not a retained raw process capture.

existing_postgres.load: Idle observation; no workload was generated.

host_observation.node_processes_excluded: Codex/tooling Node processes were not counted as server runtime.
limitations: RSS is not total committed or peak memory; macOS compression/nonresident pages and shared pages affect interpretation.
An absent named executable does not prove every possible wrapper or alias is absent; this observation does not measure a full application stack.

historical_harness.scope: Local native runtime, real proof/v0 signatures, synthetic RPC outcomes. RSS sampled after each case includes harness/prover; separate SBF scope. Approximately 295-298 MiB does not qualify 4 GiB production.

actual_bundle_proof_evidence.scope: Actual supplied-bundle native and Node WASM proof compatibility. Not a browser, full-server or memory-capacity benchmark.

findings.finding: State owns Vec<FinalizedBlock>. Open reads/deserializes/re-serializes the complete journal for checksum; every mutation clones State and serializes the complete next state before fsync/rename/directory fsync. Alerts and attempt updates also pay this history cost. Disk JSON bytes are not a direct RAM multiplier.
Decoded finalized blocks retain all transactions in the queried archive, including unrelated transactions. Quiet application usage or a fresh Pool does not stop later chain-history growth.
64-block/8-MiB limits bound only the pending append batch. A single oversized block is intentionally committed alone. Previously retained archive is never bounded by this setting.

Indexer retains one digest per accepted block for exact duplicate/fork checks. Its internal per-block optimization avoids copying this map, but outer Scanner clones copy the growing map. Archive segmentation alone leaves this RAM/copy-work growth in the challenger and retained history in the standalone indexer.
RPC call materializes response JSON and clones result without an explicit response-byte bound; up to four block reads run concurrently. Pending-batch limits do not bound this transient allocation.

Full-state rewrite temporarily needs old and next journal files. Segmentation would reduce rewrites and archive RAM, but full retained blocks, digest indexes, database/WAL, proof assets, backups and crash tails still consume storage. One 873480914-byte historical file proves neither bytes/day nor 30-day fit on 20 GiB.

design_not_implemented: Opt-in versioned archive only in a new empty directory. Preserve v1 checksum/reader/writer behavior and all historical journals. Any later migration must be explicit offline copy, independently verified, with source retained.

Immutable bounded block segments plus checksummed compact committed head. Fsync segment file and archive directory before committing/fsyncing head; install checked Scanner only after durable commit. Stream replay and use indexed slot lookup/tail/count APIs; no growing in-memory manifest.

Unreferenced crash tails are retained and never automatically adopted. Missing/tampered/reordered committed chunks, incorrect pool/version or fork fail closed; uncertain persistence poisons mutation until reopen.

Solve accepted-block digest history and Scanner clones together with an exact disk-backed digest index or separately reviewed strict-forward mode backed by verified historical lookup. Preserve default duplicate/fork semantics and all financial/buffer state.

Retain exact historical block time for payload fee planning and all signed attempts, unknown outcomes, evidence and no-replay recovery. Do not prune unresolved state or casually filter foreign transactions; transaction positions, CPI attribution and buffer generation must remain equivalent.

Separate disk design: measure bytes/slot/day and choose a budget including backlog, WAL, temporary writes, assets and backups. Evaluate lossless compression, or a versioned replay projection with verified provenance/position equivalence, or explicit retention/cold-storage rules proving all required evidence remains recoverable. No such format or deletion is authorized by this review.
Review RPC response limits/streaming and oversized-block failure semantics separately; silently rejecting or truncating valid history is not an acceptable memory fix.
required_acceptance_not_run: Generate synthetic full histories by streaming, with fixed financial activity and increasing payload history (for example 0.25, 1 and 4 GiB); measure process-tree peak, steady RSS, memory versus history slope, copy/serialization CPU, append bytes/latency, startup and lookup costs. Report financial-state growth separately.

Exercise skipped slots, large foreign payloads, CPI/buffer generations, exact old duplicates and conflicting forks. Compare legacy and new replay roots, positions, jobs, fees and signed attempt bytes.

Inject crashes/failures at each segment/head write, fsync and rename boundary; test missing/corrupt/reordered segment, uncommitted tail, no automatic adoption or resend, v1 byte compatibility, and real proof/SBF regression.

Measure bytes/slot/day over representative intervals and backlog, model data/WAL/log/backup/temporary space and recovery reserve, then substantiate 30-day disk fit. Segmentation or a single file stat cannot establish this.

Qualify exact Linux architecture and binaries with full service stack in a 4-GiB/2-vCPU cgroup, no swap, using memory.peak and child-process accounting. Include cold start, restart/replay, catch-up faster than incoming history, proof generation, gateway/control load and recovery. Record OOM/headroom/CPU-credit behavior. An 8-GiB rerun is a separate result if needed.
Measure release compile/link peaks separately on an off-host Linux builder. Verify installed hashes on the runtime host; macOS tests do not qualify Linux builds or runtime capacity.
